extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS authors and reviewers (including area chairs, senior area chairs, PC and track chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Policy guidance for reviewers and submitting authors at NeurIPS 2025 describing expectations for reciprocity, review quality, timeliness, and the specific enforcement mechanisms (withholding access and desk rejection) to uphold review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewing obligation (Submitting to NeurIPS Is a Partnership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submission needs to nominate a reciprocal reviewer from the authors and many invited reviewers also submit papers, fostering a partnership between authors-reviewers and the conference that emphasizes a reciprocal system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement frames submitting as a shared commitment: 'authors expect timely, high-quality feedback' and therefore 'reviewers—often authors themselves—must fulfill their crucial obligation to provide thorough, punctual reviews.' This sets an expectation that authors who submit should participate professionally as reviewers to sustain conference quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be submitted on time; late reviews threaten review quality and timeline and will trigger enforcement measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will receive several reminders before the reviewing deadline. Those who are also authors—and fail to submit their reviews—will be specifically alerted. In the worst case, negligent reviewers and their co-authors will lose access to reviews on their own papers for the first five days of rebuttal (access may be withheld until completion of assigned reviews, maximally until two days before the end of the authors rebuttal period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive review quality (no placeholders/low-quality reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be substantive and of sufficient quality; placeholder or otherwise low-quality reviews are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs and SACs will flag any low-quality review, such as placeholder ones, regardless of whether it’s submitted on time or late. Flagged reviewers will be notified and required to address issues; persistent significant problems can lead to sanctions (see desk rejection sanction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews Withholding Mechanism (access control for reviewer-authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who are also authors (and their co‑authors) will not see the reviews of their own submission(s) unless they have completed all assigned reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to reviews is withheld until the reviewer completes their professional reviews (withholding may last maximally until two days before the end of the authors rebuttal period). This is intended to enforce the expectation that author-reviewers complete their reviewing duties before benefiting from reviews of their own papers. Reviewers will receive multiple reminders before the deadline; those who fail to submit will be specifically alerted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk rejection sanction for gross negligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Desk rejection at the meta-review stage may be used as a last‑resort sanction against grossly negligent reviewer-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following experiences at other conferences, the policy reserves desk rejection during meta-review as a severe penalty when gross negligence is verified. ACs/SACs flag low-quality reviews and notify reviewers to address problems; if significant problems persist and are verified by the PC chairs and D&B track chairs, the reviewer's own submitted papers may face desk rejection during the meta-review stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC/SAC oversight, remediation, and verification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs (ACs) and Senior Area Chairs (SACs) will flag low-quality reviews, require remediation from the reviewer, and escalate verified persistent issues to PC and track chairs for sanction decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs and SACs will flag any low-quality review, notify the reviewer, and require fixes. If significant problems persist, verification by PC chairs and D&B track chairs is required before applying the desk-rejection sanction. This outlines an oversight and remediation workflow rather than immediate unilateral sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of measures (tracks covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the main track and the Datasets & Benchmarks (D&B) track will adopt the described safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The measures (withholding and desk-rejection sanction process) apply to both the main NeurIPS track and the D&B track, so authors/reviewers in both tracks should expect the same obligations and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of improved outcomes through shared responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The policies are intended to increase the proportion of papers receiving responsible, timely reviews by reinforcing a norm that reviewing is a partnership with NeurIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement requests reviewers to 'think about reviewing as a partnership with NeurIPS that will improve outcomes for the whole community'—this communicates an evaluative norm (professional participation) rather than a numeric scoring rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and reminder procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will receive several reminders before the reviewing deadline; author-reviewers who fail to submit will receive specific alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural element supports enforcement: multiple reminders are part of the mechanism to encourage compliance before access withholding or escalation.
